title: Hanford complete material balance receives long-term retention and inactive-by-default recovery
summary: Bounded retention and append-only tombstones keep retired artifacts discoverable but inactive; authorized restore drills verify exact digests without changing reader state; and disaster recovery remains reversible with notice, grace, and rollback intact. Denominator: One recovery schema, thirty-two adversarial cases, eight bounded preservation routes, twenty-four explicit rejections, and zero production tombstones, restorations, reader migrations, or disaster events.
key_findings: Evidence stage: Long-term legacy retention, tombstone, discoverability, and disaster-recovery controls.
